title: Descent of lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaves and their morphisms
statement:
Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme.

1. For every lisse $\QbarX$-module $L$ there are a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a lisse $E_X$-module
   $L_E$ and an isomorphism $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}L_E\cong L$.
2. For lisse $E_X$-modules $M,N$, the map
   $\varinjlim_{F\supseteq E}\Hom_{F_X}(M_F,N_F)\to\Hom_{\QbarX}(M_{\Qlb},N_{\Qlb})$ is bijective.

Coefficient and locality conventions: fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Finite coefficient fields are the subextensions inside this closure [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Work on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Here $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring], and $\QbarX=p_X^*\underline{\Qlb}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], where $\underline{\Qlb}$ is the condensed ring whose continuous sections have values in a finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. The inclusions are [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map] and [def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map]. Modules and their linear maps are the module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. A module over a ring sheaf $A$ is lisse here if on a covering $\{V_i\to X\}$ its restrictions to the slice sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] are isomorphic to $(A|_{V_i})^{r_i}$ with each $r_i$ a finite nonnegative integer. Thus rank zero and varying local ranks are allowed. Scalar extension means the ordinary relative tensor product [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; $M_F=F_X\otimes_{E_X}M$ and $M_{\Qlb}=\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}M$, and similarly for $N$. The index in (2) is the directed poset of finite $F$ containing the given finite $E$; transition maps on Hom are scalar extension. The displayed colimit is the set of representatives $(F,\phi_F)$ modulo the equivalence generated by scalar extension to a larger field. Quasi-compact means that $X$ has a finite affine open cover, and quasi-separated has the diagonal meaning of [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

proof.text: Apply the finite lisse object model theorem, which carries steps 1--5 of the original proof and their geometric descent argument.
Apply finite-stage lifting of lisse morphisms and package the field, inclusion and morphism as a sigma-type representative. This proves surjectivity.

The coefficient-linear projection constructed in SplitCoefficientDerivedFaithful splits the extension-restriction adjunction unit. Naturality of this unit and its splitting proves faithfulness on ordinary module objects, without lisse or qcqs hypotheses. Conjugation by the canonical comparisons therefore makes each representative comparison injective.

Derive associativity of the canonical extension comparisons from uniqueness of left adjoints and the strictly compatible restriction comparisons. This gives invariance of the algebraic-closure image under every Hom transition. For two representatives with equal images choose the finite compositum of their fields. Their transitions there have equal images; faithfulness makes them equal. The two generating relations give an EqvGen zigzag. Conversely induct on EqvGen, using transition invariance, reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity of equality.

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)--(2), with ordinary coefficient faithfulness from the existing split-unit construction
proof_origin.note: F1: both object descent and finite-stage Hom lifting are proved from existing interfaces. Canonical comparison coherence, ordinary scalar faithfulness and the representative equivalence relation are fully proved; no new sorry remains.

split_report.summary: Completed the transition-matrix argument for both clauses using existing coefficient-section descent, module-sheaf descent and morphism-gluing nodes. Made all coefficient and locality conventions explicit; handled varying and zero ranks, finite common affine covers, quasi-compact pair/triple overlaps, inverse matrices, and Hom representatives at distinct finite fields. Corrected the false repeated-index identity in the blueprint proof; no conclusion or hypothesis changed and no new node was needed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes Proof (1) of det-lem-coefficient-finite-descent-lisse and clause (1) of sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit by steps 1-5; realizes Proof (2), lisse morphism descent, by steps 6-7. The same transition-matrix route is kept.

tool_uses.why: General effective descent for module sheaves on an arbitrary site supplies the gluing of finite free local models; this is the descent of sheaves invoked by the unit, not a substitute for coefficient descent.
General gluing and uniqueness of module-sheaf morphisms supplies the final local-to-global maps and equality tests; the unit has no separate morphism-gluing theorem.
Defines the sectionwise sheaf tensor used to spell out the pure-tensor calculations; it agrees with the relative coequalizer in the coefficient unit by the balanced bilinear universal property.
Only the axioms for composing and pulling back covers are used to form a common trivializing cover.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-e18bbe8e6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 14 proof dependencies and 11 statement dependencies, the main-20261015 lemma and its proof, the unit proof and record, the meaning of lisse in sk-lem-coefficient-heart, and Stacks 0989, 04TQ and 04TR. Statement: the qcqs hypothesis and both clauses are verbatim from main-20261015. The conventions paragraph only makes explicit what the blueprint leaves implicit: E_X and QbarX as pulled-back condensed rings, module objects in Sh(X_proet,Ab) (the upstream ModuleObject category), scalar extension as the relative coequalizer, and lisse as pro-etale locally finite free with rank 0 and varying ranks allowed. Nothing is weakened. Step 1: the finite affine family is a covering by qcqs-permanence (1), since V_i is affine and X quasi-separated, together with the fpqc clause, and pair and triple overlaps are quasi-compact by (3) then (2). Step 2 (local algebra) is correctly marked elementary: it covers matrices on a slice, the comparison of internal and sectionwise modules and of the coequalizer and balanced tensor, compatibility of sheafification with slices, and a correctly typed transitivity formula. Step 3: the entries of g_ij and their inverses descend on the quasi-compact V_ij by sections node (2); composita give one E (Q_l if there are no entries); injectivity gives the inverse and cocycle identities. The source error is genuine: the blueprint's g_kk=1 fails for non-monomorphic covers. I checked the counterexample X=Spec k, V=X⊔X, where the cross component carries the matrix 2, and Stacks 04TR imposes no such identity. Steps 4 and 5: site module gluing with U=X; I checked that the local maps b_i=t_i^{-1}(e_i)_Qbar agree on overlaps, and the inverse is glued with uniqueness. Steps 6 and 7: rectangular matrices with overlap equation u^N A_i = A_j u^M descend to a common F containing E, and injectivity is proved at a compositum H. Edge cases checked: empty X, rank 0, unequal ranks on a disconnected cover, the self-overlap example. There are no new nodes and no duplicate was found. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing and lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing (generic sheaf descent and morphism gluing, which the unit invokes); the other two entries are definitions. No SGA is used. No fixes.

lean.note: Uses the already landed IsLisseCoefficientModule, adding its owning node to stmt_deps. Clause (2) is stated exactly by representatives for the specified set colimit: the canonical representative map is surjective and its kernel equivalence is Relation.EqvGen of scalar extension. The backward implication includes well-definedness and the forward implication includes injectivity of the induced quotient map. The six helper declarations supply only these representatives and their canonical ordinary tensor comparisons; no arbitrary comparison or derived scalar extension is used.
